title: Collibra visual capability catalog
implementation_boundary: This is a framework-neutral visual contract. Products and document producers own the implementation, asset files, export settings, and medium-specific validation.
source_policy: Use measured token values and cited source artifacts. When the source does not publish a value or asset, use the defined consumer-boundary contract instead of guessing or implying a shared default.
principles: Make the hierarchy visible before adding decoration.
Use the approved palette by semantic role, then verify contrast in the actual context.
Treat typography, spacing, shape, imagery, and motion as communication tools rather than polish layers.
Translate the system across products and media without pretending that one implementation is universal.
Show uncertainty, provenance, and status in text and structure; never make color carry the meaning alone.
Prefer a small, adoptable visual language over a large catalog nobody can maintain.

foundations.name: Color palette and semantic roles
foundations.purpose: Provide the approved brand palette and the role-based references used by UI, UX, documents, and visual communication.
foundations.contract: Consume color through tokens. Use primary navy and lime for primary brand expression, forest and light forest for supporting roles, and neutrals for readable surfaces and text. Ramp steps are for illustration and data visualization only unless a contrast check proves another use safe.

foundations.name: Typography and type hierarchy
foundations.purpose: Give every surface a readable, recognizable hierarchy that can be translated to web, presentations, and document outputs.
foundations.contract: Use the published display family for web and creative work, Arial for presentations, and Roboto Mono only for all-caps eyebrows and tags. Use the measured web and slide scales by medium; do not silently substitute a scale from another medium.
open_questions: Confirm the conflicting headline and body letter-spacing labels with the brand team before treating them as web defaults.

foundations.name: Contrast and accessible color use
foundations.purpose: Make readable, perceivable communication the default across component states, diagrams, charts, and branded surfaces.
foundations.contract: Meet the published WCAG AA thresholds for body and large or bold text. Test the foreground, background, state, and size in the actual composition. Preserve a non-color cue for status, selection, error, and difference.

foundations.name: Surface and corner treatment
foundations.purpose: Keep containers, panels, controls, and cards visually related without introducing an unapproved radius ramp.
foundations.contract: Use the single published radius token for container-like elements when the medium supports it. Treat radius as a role, not an opportunity to add arbitrary shape variation.

foundations.name: Spacing and composition rhythm
foundations.purpose: Define repeatable relationships between content, controls, regions, and visual landmarks once an approved scale exists.
foundations.contract: Use the consuming product or medium's spacing system as the implementation source. Document the mapping between content, controls, regions, and landmarks, preserve hierarchy at the smallest supported viewport, and do not claim a shared Collibra numeric scale where none is published.

foundations.name: Gradients and tonal fields
foundations.purpose: Give teams a safe decision path for gradient-led brand compositions without fabricating unpublished stops.
foundations.contract: Use flat navy or an approved raster asset when a gradient source file is unavailable. If a consumer has an approved gradient, record its source, direction, stop values, contrast behavior, and fallback before using it; palette ramps alone do not create an official Collibra gradient.

capabilities.name: Logo and mark usage
capabilities.purpose: Protect the Collibra mark, clear space, lockups, sizing, and export behavior wherever the brand is identified.
capabilities.contract: Use the approved logo package from the governed brand source. Keep clear space, lockup, minimum-size, background, color, export, and accessibility treatment tied to that package; this repo defines the usage boundary and reference, not a duplicate asset distribution.

capabilities.name: Color application
capabilities.purpose: Turn the palette into a legible hierarchy of surfaces, text, actions, links, tags, charts, and illustration accents.
capabilities.contract: Start from semantic role, check contrast, and keep ramp values out of text and controls unless the use is explicitly tested and approved.

capabilities.name: Type pairing and hierarchy
capabilities.purpose: Make the reading order, action hierarchy, metadata, and brand voice visible through type rather than decoration.
capabilities.contract: Select a medium-specific scale, pair it with the correct family, keep the line length readable, and do not use the mono family as general body copy.
open_questions: Confirm font licensing and runtime delivery expectations for products that cannot ship the published display family.

capabilities.name: Iconography
capabilities.purpose: Create a coherent supporting language for navigation, status, action, and object concepts.
capabilities.contract: Choose one consumer-owned icon family per surface and document stroke or fill, optical sizing, licensing, export, accessible naming, and non-color cues with the product owner. Pair unfamiliar icons with visible text; this suite defines the selection and accessibility rule, not a single shared Collibra icon package.

capabilities.name: Illustration and graphic motifs
capabilities.purpose: Give campaigns, empty states, education, and explanatory surfaces a recognizable visual vocabulary.
capabilities.contract: Use an approved motif or consumer-owned illustration set only after its palette roles, composition, accessibility text treatment, provenance, review owner, and usage authority are recorded. This suite defines the adoption checklist and does not distribute an unlicensed motif library.

capabilities.name: Photography and imagery
capabilities.purpose: Set expectations for subject, crop, treatment, captioning, alt text, and rights when photography or editorial imagery is used.
capabilities.contract: Use photography or editorial imagery only when the source, rights or usage authority, crop treatment, caption or alt-text treatment, review owner, and removal path are recorded. Treat stock or synthetic examples as examples, never as shared Collibra assets.

capabilities.name: Diagram and information graphics
capabilities.purpose: Make systems, relationships, decisions, and process states understandable without turning every diagram into a one-off composition.
capabilities.contract: Use the diagram-theme-suite semantic roles for shapes, connectors, direction, legends, readable labels, source notes, and non-color distinctions. Keep the diagram's claim no broader than its evidence and let the consuming medium own geometry and delivery.

capabilities.name: Diagram and workflow theme suite
capabilities.purpose: Give diagram, workflow, chart, and information-graphic producers one semantic Collibra theming contract that can translate across presentations, documents, product surfaces, and exported media.
capabilities.contract: Use the theme suite's token-backed semantic roles for surfaces, entities, boundaries, actions, decisions, states, evidence, unknowns, flows, handoffs, dependencies, exceptions, and boundary crossings. Preserve labels, direction, source context, accessibility summaries, and non-color cues; consumers own layout geometry, export settings, and native validation. State comparison consumers may use the state_comparison layout treatment for explicit legacy, transitional, target, and retirement columns; journey consumers may use the journey rail; quadrant consumers may use the two-axis decision field; pyramid consumers may use the foundation-to-outcome stack; and refinement-tier consumers may use the medallion treatment for one artifact moving through quality states with explicit promotion gates, without implying live discovery.

capabilities.name: Data visualization
capabilities.purpose: Help people compare, inspect, and decide from data while preserving meaning, scale, provenance, and uncertainty.
capabilities.contract: Use ramp values for visual encoding only after contrast and distinguishability checks. Label axes and units, provide a text or table alternative when needed, and make source and time context inspectable.
open_questions: Define chart families, color sequencing, annotation conventions, and minimum data-label requirements.

capabilities.name: Slide visual grammar suite
capabilities.purpose: Give slide and document producers a reader-first way to choose varied visual forms, shells, and editorial rhythm without treating a renderer or template layout as the design system.
capabilities.contract: Choose a named grammar from the reader question, preserve its reading order, accessibility cue, evidence contract, and cross-medium translation, then let the consuming library own geometry, native template inheritance, export, and final-medium validation. Add a new atom only when the input contract or visual grammar is genuinely distinct; otherwise add a governed recipe or story arc.

capabilities.name: Motion and transition
capabilities.purpose: Use movement to explain change, continuity, progress, and feedback without distracting from the task or excluding users.
capabilities.contract: Motion must have a communication purpose, respect reduced-motion preferences, avoid implying progress that is not measured, and keep all state changes available without animation.
open_questions: Define motion principles, timing tokens, reduced-motion behavior, and product-specific exceptions.

capabilities.name: Surfaces, borders, and shape
capabilities.purpose: Create clear grouping and depth using approved surfaces, hairlines, and the published corner treatment.
capabilities.contract: Use neutral surfaces for reading and role-based accents for emphasis. Use the single radius token for container-like elements and do not add a shadow or border solely for ornament.
open_questions: Confirm shadow, border, elevation, and panel treatments for product and document contexts.

capabilities.name: Reader-first document composition
capabilities.purpose: Give branded documents a recognizable reading path without turning every paragraph into decoration or forcing one layout onto every audience.
capabilities.contract: Begin with the answer, outcome, or decision the reader needs. Use token-backed navy headings, readable neutral body text, a light base, restrained supporting panels, forest links, and lime only as a safe accent or fill. Use cards for real groupings, tables for real comparisons, numbered lists for sequences, and diagrams or images only when they explain a relationship or example faster than prose. Keep paragraph rhythm open, preserve a readable type floor, and let the document consumer own exact type sizes and spacing until an approved Docs scale exists. Use native tabs only for distinct, durable reader tasks; preserve the complete tab tree when adapting an existing document. Verify the final native document and exported pages, including alt text, link behavior, contrast, page breaks, and non-color meaning.
open_questions: Approve a shared Google Docs type and spacing scale before treating one consumer recipe as a universal numeric default.

capabilities.name: Visual accessibility
capabilities.purpose: Make visual communication perceivable, operable, and understandable across contrast, type, focus, motion, and non-color cues.
capabilities.contract: Use the tokenized contrast thresholds, preserve readable type hierarchy, maintain visible focus, provide alternatives to color and motion, and test the final medium rather than trusting a token pairing in isolation.

capabilities.name: Asset provenance and lifecycle
capabilities.purpose: Make shared visual assets trustworthy, findable, reviewable, and removable when their source or rights change.
capabilities.contract: Every shared asset needs an owner, source, license or usage authority, version, review date, alt-text or accessibility treatment, and a clear deprecation path. This repo records contracts and references; it does not become an ungoverned asset dump.

capabilities.name: Governed program brand extensions
capabilities.purpose: Let an internal program develop a recognizable identity that remains traceable to the Collibra visual system without replacing the corporate brand or leaking private assets into public distribution.
capabilities.contract: A program extension must name its owner, purpose, maturity, semantic token roles, visual motifs, provenance, usage authority, accessibility treatment, channel rules, review states, version, and deprecation path. Keep the shared adoption contract public-safe while private program assets and restricted source links stay in the governed private extension and Drive collection. Consumers must label proposed work, preserve visible text and non-color meaning, and complete the recorded brand, legal, accessibility, and owner reviews before external publication or a corporate-brand claim.

capabilities.name: Cross-medium translation
capabilities.purpose: Keep the brand recognizable as a composition moves between product UI, web, presentations, documents, and data outputs.
capabilities.contract: Start with the canonical token and semantic role, then select the medium-specific type scale, layout system, export constraints, and accessibility check. Record any exception instead of silently forking the standard.
open_questions: Document the approved translation matrix for product UI, web, Slides, Docs, Sheets, and exported PDF.

capabilities.name: Responsive composition
capabilities.purpose: Preserve hierarchy, task actions, and readable content as a composition changes viewport, density, or medium.
capabilities.contract: Use consumer-owned layout and spacing rules until the shared scale is approved. Test the smallest supported viewport and the densest supported content; never let decoration displace the primary task.
open_questions: Approve shared responsive breakpoints or a medium-neutral composition rule set.

capabilities.name: Theme and mode translation
capabilities.purpose: Define how the Collibra visual language adapts to product themes or light and dark modes without inventing unapproved palette roles.
capabilities.contract: Light-theme Collibra primitives are the shared baseline. Consumers own dark or alternate-mode mappings; when a consumer adds one, measure foreground, surface, status, chart, focus, and disabled roles, preserve non-color cues, and record the mapping and contrast checks with the product owner. This suite does not claim a universal dark theme.
